hook: SCP-752 is a hidden underground city of about ten thousand people bred to be an ideal society. Most of the story is told through diary entries left by its creators, a group calling itself Eudaimon, and each entry carries a population count at the top, so keep an eye on how fast that number climbs. The logs describe cannibalism, the killing of the weak and people working themselves to death.
whyItMatters:
This is a utopia story told from the lab bench. The creators get exactly the selfless, cooperative people they designed, and the article lets you watch that success turn into something they cannot stomach.

The framing also keeps the Foundation at a distance until the very end. Its own stake is stated only in the last lines, where the fear is not cruelty inside the city but what would happen if its people ever met ours.
thingsToNotice:
The inhabitants have no self-interest at all, and that is where every horror comes from: the dead are eaten, the frail die by suicide or are killed, and a merit-based caste system has workers laboring willingly until they drop, cutting a 150-year potential lifespan to about 45. Their only culture is a strict faith in the Eudaimon who will one day return and lead them to another world, which the creators planted on purpose. Beta-4's realization that none of this is deviance, because the society contains no deviance, is the article's turning point.

Alpha-1's entry shows he is pleased, expects them to reach his own level before the planned release, and is hiding what goes on in the nurseries. Gamma is killed trying to intervene, a coup against Alpha follows, Alpha-3 poisons most of Beta, and three of the Alphas escape; the survivors disable the release mechanism and leave the inhabitants believing nothing exists beyond the shield.

The Foundation's probe finds an apparently voluntary, expunged procedure in the nurseries before conception, goes dark within hours, and its technology is in wide use in the city within two months. The file ends by warning that open competition with humanity would mean an SK-class dominance shift, so the city must never learn there is an outside.
